text:
ariel (support): Hey team — customer jubilant-ops is reporting streaming responses that stop mid-token and then a client reconnect that results in duplicated tokens and billing counting partial+resume tokens. Root report: https://app.support/INC-8942. They attached a pcap and server logs.

customer:jubilant-ops: FYI we see it reproducible from our side. Using our JS client we get output cut at ~120 tokens, then a reconnect, then the rest starts but repeats last ~8 tokens. Billing shows two partial responses. Happening ~3-4x/day.

zara (support-esc): Thanks, can you paste a minimal repro? Node client + options, and the exact headers you receive on resume?

customer:jubilant-ops: Repro snippet:

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","prompt":"write a 200-token paragraph...","stream":true}' \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
```

We see SSE events: data: {"token":"..."}. Client auto reconnects with Last-Event-ID: <last-id>.

ariel (support): Good. I pulled the pcap they attached. Quick notes in case someone wants to look: tcp FINs from upstream around the cut, TLS renegotiation entries right before. I'll paste the relevant tcpdump extract.

```
17:12:43.123456 IP client->lb TLS Application Data length: 512
17:12:43.223789 IP lb->upstream TLS Application Data length: 1024
17:12:43.223790 IP upstream -> lb TCP RST
17:12:43.223795 IP upstream -> lb [RST] Sequence=0 Ack=0
```

mike (eng-runtime): Thanks. Quick hypothesis: upstream model-worker closed the TCP connection mid-stream (RST) — causes SSE to cut. Client reconnects and resumes but server-side resume logic appears to re-send overlapping tokens. Also billing saw tokens counted across both connections.

sana (eng-infra): FYI I correlated the request_id from their logs with our observability: request_id=rid_0a9c. Streaming.latency and streaming.bytes show a spike then an abrupt end. Nginx proxy shows proxy_buffering on and proxy_read_timeout hitting at 120s in a few of these. There's also an intermittent GC pause in the model-worker logs around the same time.

mike (eng-runtime): Possible factors: 1) model-worker GC pause triggers it to not read from socket -> OS buffers fill -> upstream resets. 2) proxy buffering could cause delayed flush semantics so client Last-Event-ID is misaligned. 3) resume protocol isn't deduping the overlap.

zara (support-esc): Customer asked for mitigation now. Can we produce a short list of steps they can take to reduce impact while we patch?

mike (eng-runtime): Short-term for customer: 1) set client to use exponential backoff + jitter for reconnects (avoid immediate resume). 2) include a small overlap token-skip on resume (client drop N tokens if duplication seen). 3) enable SSE heartbeat on server side (we already support ping events; recommend enabling keepalive every 15s).

ariel (support): Also suggest they upgrade to the JS client 1.4.2 which has resume_id handling that avoids double-ack in most cases. Provide command: `npm i @redwood/client@1.4.2`.

customer:jubilant-ops: We tried backoff but still see duplicates occasionally. We can share the full pcap privately.

sana (eng-infra): Please share pcap. In parallel I'll check infra metrics. From the observability dashboard: model-worker GC 99th percentile rose to 1.6s in the window. network drop counters show small increase of TLS connections churn. I'll trigger a debug trace for the specific backend pool.

deploy-bot: Started trace capture for pool redwood-prod-3b at 2028-05-03T17:20:30Z trace_id=trace-4b2f.

mike (eng-runtime): I pulled the worker logs around rid_0a9c: there's a minor OOM-suspect GC where the python process paused for ~950ms, then resumed and dropped the socket (close-with-RST path). That's consistent with the RST in the pcap. The streaming runtime currently treats any connection restart as a fresh send unless the resume token sequence matches exactly; it doesn't amortize overlap ranges.

zara (support-esc): So root cause: intermittent worker pause -> connection closed -> client reconnect -> resume duplicates. Side effect: billing counts tokens both sides. Any quick fix for billing counting?

mike (eng-runtime): On billing side our event ingestion increments tokens on chunk finalization. If a partial stream didn't send a finalization marker (we rely on end-of-stream), both partial and resumed segments get counted. Short term: we can implement dedupe in billing downstream matching request_id + token_id ranges, but that's not instant. For immediate relief we can offer a billing credit for affected invoices if we confirm duplication.

ariel (support): I'll open a billing case and offer provisional credit while engineering investigates. Customer, would you like that?

customer:jubilant-ops: Yes please — credits would help. We'll send pcap and the client debug logs.

sana (eng-infra): For infra mitigation I'm going to: 1) adjust nginx proxy_read_timeout from 120s -> 300s for stream endpoints to avoid proxy triggering on long tokens, 2) disable proxy_buffering for /v1/streams paths, 3) increase keepalive to keep sockets open. We should monitor memory pressure; proxy timeout change is conservative.

mike (eng-runtime): On runtime side I'll push a small change to stream resume semantics: when client sends Last-Event-ID we will compare last N token suffix and if overlap detected we'll drop duplicates server-side (idempotent token replay). Also will add a small invariant emission: finalization markers are flushed immediately after each chunk so billing can decide on partial vs final. I'll open PR with tests.

mike (eng-runtime): Draft quickfix PR:

```python
# in stream_handler.py
if resume_id:
    overlap = find_overlap(prev_tokens, resume_tokens)
    if overlap > 0:
        skip_first_n = overlap
    # ensure we emit FINAL_LINE after each chunk
    emit('\u0004')  # EOT marker for billing consumers
```

zara (support-esc): Nice. Timeline?

mike (eng-runtime): I'll cut a patch to canary within the next 6 hours and roll to 5% of streaming traffic. If metrics look good (no regressions in latency/higher CPU) we'll roll wider in 24h.

sana (eng-infra): I'll also add a GC telemetry alert to monitor worker pause >500ms in the 1m window and raise to oncall.

ariel (support): Customer-facing summary I'll send: - What happened: intermittent worker pause caused connection reset so client reconnected and resumed, leading to duplicated tokens and double-billing. - Short term mitigations: enable client backoff, enable server heartbeats, upgrade client library, we applied nginx buffer/read_timeout tuning to preserve long streams. - Medium term fixes: runtime dedupe on resume and billing dedupe logic; canary in progress. - Next steps: pcap + logs from customer, billing credit offer, ETA for canary.

customer:jubilant-ops: Thanks. We'll drop the pcap into the ticket and confirm we want credits. Also curious if there is a way to ensure our app never shows duplicates — we'll try client-side skip logic as well.

ariel (support): Great. Can you also send the exact Last-Event-ID header values you see on reconnect? That will help match.

customer:jubilant-ops: Will do. Sharing now.

mike (eng-runtime): Action items: (1) me: PR for dedupe and finalization marker (in review), (2) sana: nginx config change deployed to staging + GC alert, (3) ariel/zara: handle billing credit and confirm pcap received.

sana (eng-infra): Deployed nginx change to staging and ran a replay against the pcap: buffering off + longer timeouts prevented premature close in 95% of replays. Rolling to prod in 30m behind canary.

deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated: nginx-config-streams-v2 -> 3% traffic.

mike (eng-runtime): Canary build for runtime dedupe pushed to staging. I will coordinate with infra for a staggered rollout after nginx canary stabilizes.

zara (support-esc): I'll update the ticket with the mitigation steps and the canary ETA. Customer notified.

ariel (support): Closing loop: If customer confirms duplicates stop after the changes, we'll finalize billing credits and close. If they still see issues, escalate to P1. Thanks everyone for fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
